The (Ga,Fe)N layers were grown by MOVPE on GaN buffer layers on sapphire substrates.
HRXRD analysis identified the presence of α-Fe and γ'-GayFe4-yN nanocrystal phases in the films.
The size of the nanocrystals was estimated to be 17±2 nm for α-Fe and 22±2 nm for γ'-GayFe4-yN.
Annealing of the uncapped sample removed the α-Fe nanocrystals and led to the formation of polycrystalline FeOx at the surface.
The magnetic response of the films is dominated by a superparamagnetic-like contribution from the nanocrystals and a paramagnetic contribution from dilute Fe3+ ions in the GaN matrix.
The coercive field values of 10-60 mT are consistent with the presence of ferromagnetic γ'-Fe4N nanocrystals.
FMR measurements confirmed the uniaxial out-of-plane and in-plane hexagonal anisotropy of the nanocrystals.
The resistivity of the capped sample (Sample B) is enhanced by 3 orders of magnitude below 100K compared to the other samples, attributed to compensation of the GaN matrix by diffusion of Fe.
The transition from Arrhenius to Mott variable range hopping conduction occurs between 50-130K, depending on the sample.
The anisotropic magnetoresistance shows positive values throughout the 2-300K temperature range, one order of magnitude higher than for γ'-Fe4N thin films.
The hysteretic behavior in the magnetoresistance at low fields is attributed to spin-polarized transport between the nanocrystals below 25K.
The localization length ξ obtained from the magnetoresistance data is in the range of 7-10 nm, with hopping distances Rh between 30-70 nm.
The AMR is not observed in the GaN reference layer, confirming it originates from the embedded nanocrystals.
The magnetotransport properties are significantly affected by the presence and characteristics of the embedded nanocrystals.
Capping the (Ga,Fe)N layer with GaN leads to diffusion of Fe into the capping layer, altering the transport behavior.
